pages.text: A signal reaches another station two ways:$(li)$(thing)Line of sight$(): out to a range set by the band (2 m about 500 blocks), fading with distance. High ground sees further: two masts 6 blocks above the land around them get the band's range, a hilltop station much more, two handhelds on flat ground about half.$(li)$(thing)Skip$(): HF bounces off the sky and comes down far away, in a window of distances that differs by band and between day and night. In between is a silent zone.

pages.title: Each band's job
pages.text: $(li)$(thing)80 m$(): close and regional, never a silent zone; furthest at night.$(li)$(thing)40 m$(): the daytime workhorse; at night it goes long and loses the middle distances to 80 m.$(li)$(thing)20 m$(): far away by day, weak at night.$(li)$(thing)10 m$(): a short opening in average weather, far when the sun is lively; also good locally.$(li)$(thing)2 m$(): local, repeaters and satellites.

pages.title: Which band?
pages.text: Up to 1,000 blocks: 80 or 40 m by day, 80 m at night. To 2,000: 40 m by day, 80 m at night. To 4,000: 20 m by day, 40 or 80 m at night. Further: 20 m by day, 40 m at night.$(br2)The radio computer's $(thing)PREDICT$() shows which bands open to a place over the next day; admins can use $(thing)/bandcalculate <from> <to>$().

pages.title: More than one hop
pages.text: When 10, 20 or 40 m is open (fair or better), skip can bounce off the ground and up again: two hops reach twice as far, three hops three times, each hop leaving about half the signal.$(br2)Each hop leaves at the angle that reaches the sky half way along it: a short hop goes nearly straight up, a long one skims the horizon.

pages.title: Commercial bands
pages.text: Besides the ham bands there are two commercial ones. $(thing)Low band$() (30-50 MHz) sits between 10 m and VHF: by line of sight it reaches a little further than 2 m and not as far as 10 m, and it skips with 10 m, by day only. $(thing)Commercial VHF$() (150-174 MHz, with the marine channels) travels like 2 m. See the $(l:radiocraft:propagation/band_plan)Band Plan$() for who uses what.
Being a few kHz off still lets you hear SSB, sounding higher or lower and thinner; 11 kHz off, nothing. FM is heard up to 2 kHz off.
pages.title: Off frequency

pages.text: Hills in the way weaken line of sight: badly on 2 m, less on 10 m and CB, least on 80 m, and HF also loses some at every cliff. Skip needs a clear view up at its hop's angle: a station deep in a valley loses long, low hops over the valley walls but keeps short, steep ones. A handheld indoors or underground is weaker. RF passes through wood planks, slabs, glass, wool and leaves. Build high!
pages.title: Hills and valleys
Server settings
pages.text: Admins can change every band's ranges in the server config, or scale them all at once with $(thing)band_range_multiplier$() (line of sight, silent zone and skip together). The radio horizon, hops and bounce height are under Terrain and Skip.
